models.notes: Text-conditioned speech, nonverbal sounds and some music generation.

models.name: Chatterbox
models.architecture: Speech-token LM and acoustic decoder
models.notes: Family of reference-conditioned speech synthesizers; capabilities vary by release.

sources.title: resemble-ai/chatterbox — official repository

models.description: Chatterbox synthesizes speech from text and a voice reference, with controls for expressive delivery. Its multilingual models focus on cross-language voice consistency, while Turbo and Nano use a smaller backbone and a single-step acoustic decoder. These variants serve different narration, conversational playback and local-device requirements; their capabilities are not interchangeable.

models.name: ChatTTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive speech-token generation
models.notes: Synthesizes conversational delivery from supplied text; does not itself answer a user's questions.

sources.title: 2noise/ChatTTS — official repository

models.architecture: Probabilistic residual quantization and multi-token LM
models.notes: Predicts multiple codec tokens jointly to reduce generation cost.

sources.title: CLaM-TTS: Improving Neural Codec Language Model for Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech

models.name: CosyVoice
models.architecture: Supervised semantic tokens and flow decoder
models.notes: Text-conditioned multilingual synthesis and voice conditioning.

sources.title: CosyVoice: A Scalable Multilingual Zero-shot Text-to-speech Synthesizer based on Supervised Semantic Tokens

models.name: CosyVoice 2
models.architecture: Text/speech LM and chunk-aware flow matching
models.notes: Supports streaming text input and audio output.

sources.title: CosyVoice 2: Scalable Streaming Speech Synthesis with Large Language Models

models.name: CosyVoice 3
models.architecture: Scaled speech LM and post-training
models.notes: Extends coverage and control of the CosyVoice streaming synthesis line.

sources.title: CosyVoice 3: Towards In-the-wild Speech Generation via Scaling-up and Post-training
CosyVoice — official implementation
CosyVoice 3 author demo

models.description: CosyVoice 3 extends streaming, reference-conditioned synthesis with a tokenizer trained on several speech-understanding tasks and a reward model for post-training. It targets reliable pronunciation, speaker identity and prosody across languages, dialects and less controlled text. The research scaling experiments and the downloadable Fun-CosyVoice3 checkpoint represent different model configurations.

models.name: CSM
models.architecture: Llama backbone and Mimi-code decoder
models.notes: Conversational Speech Model renders speech from text and audio context; the public checkpoint is not a complete voice assistant.

sources.title: sesameailabs/csm — official repository

models.description: CSM uses the text and audio of preceding speaker turns to shape the delivery of the next utterance. A Llama backbone predicts speech representations, and a smaller decoder completes Mimi audio codes. It is a contextual speech renderer: an application supplies the words to say, including any responses written by a separate language model.

models.name: Dia
models.architecture: Dialogue-conditioned codec generation
models.notes: Renders a speaker-tagged script into multi-speaker speech with optional audio context.

sources.title: nari-labs/dia — official repository

models.description: Dia turns a speaker-tagged transcript into conversational audio, including supported nonverbal events such as laughter and coughing. Reference audio and its transcript can establish speaker identity and delivery. Its English checkpoint is useful for scripted exchanges and dialogue narration, with the conversation content supplied by the user rather than generated by the model.

models.name: Dia2
models.architecture: Streaming dialogue TTS
models.notes: Starts synthesis from partial text and supports audio prefix conditioning.

sources.title: nari-labs/dia2 — official repository

models.description: Dia2 begins synthesizing before the complete script is available, allowing an application to feed words incrementally. Audio prefixes provide speaker and conversational context, while a streaming codec path reconstructs the output. The released 1B and 2B checkpoints focus on English dialogue; prefix conditioning helps keep voices consistent between generations.

models.name: ELLA-V
models.architecture: Alignment-guided token reordering
models.notes: Interleaves phonemes and acoustic codes to stabilize autoregressive synthesis.

sources.title: ELLA-V: Stable Neural Codec Language Modeling with Alignment-guided Sequence Reordering

models.name: FireRedTTS
models.architecture: Text-to-semantic LM and speech decoder
models.notes: Foundation TTS system for expressive and reference-conditioned speech.

sources.title: FireRedTTS: A Foundation Text-To-Speech Framework for Industry-Level Generative Speech Applications

models.name: FireRedTTS-2
models.architecture: Low-rate streaming codec and dialogue LM
models.notes: Generates context-aware multi-speaker speech from dialogue text.

sources.title: FireRedTTS-2: Towards Long Conversational Speech Generation for Podcast and Chatbot
FireRedTTS-2 author repository

models.description: FireRedTTS-2 models chronological sequences of speaker-labeled text and speech using a large Transformer plus a smaller codebook decoder. A low-rate streaming tokenizer reduces the number of audio steps. It targets long conversations and podcasts where speaker changes, turn-specific delivery and continuity across utterances matter.

models.name: Fish Audio S1 / OpenAudio S1
models.architecture: Dual-autoregressive speech language model
models.notes: Expressive TTS family also known as OpenAudio S1; the model card distinguishes the full S1 model and distilled S1-mini.

sources.title: fishaudio/s1-mini · Hugging Face

models.description: The S1 family combines multilingual voice conditioning with explicit markers for emotion, tone and nonverbal sounds. Its full model and distilled S1-mini offer different deployment sizes, with reinforcement learning used to refine generation. It is suited to expressive narration and character dialogue, although access and capabilities depend on the selected release.

models.name: Fish Audio S2
models.architecture: Dual-autoregressive speech modeling
models.notes: Instruction-controlled multi-speaker, multi-turn speech synthesis.

sources.title: Fish Audio S2 Technical Report
fishaudio/fish-speech — official repository

models.description: Fish Audio S2 extends the Fish speech-model line with natural-language delivery instructions and multi-speaker, multi-turn synthesis. Its training pipeline uses speech descriptions, quality assessment and reward modeling to improve controllability. The released inference stack supports streaming, making the model relevant to both scripted audio production and incremental spoken responses.

models.name: Fish Speech
models.architecture: Dual-autoregressive slow/fast transformers
models.notes: Separates semantic sequence modeling from grouped acoustic-token prediction.

sources.title: Fish-Speech: Leveraging Large Language Models for Advanced Multilingual Text-to-Speech Synthesis
fishaudio/fish-speech — official repository

models.name: Gemini 2.5 TTS
models.architecture: Gemini-derived text-to-speech
models.notes: Specialized speech-generation endpoints; separate from the Live API.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash text-to-speech | Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
Gemini 2.5 Pro text-to-speech | Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
Speech generation (text-to-speech) | Gemini API

models.description: Gemini 2.5 TTS converts supplied text into speech with prompt-based control of accent, pace, style and emotion. The Flash and Pro interfaces support single-speaker narration and two-speaker scripts with separately assigned voices. These are dedicated speech-generation endpoints; their internal acoustic architecture is not fully disclosed in the public documentation.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS
models.architecture: Gemini-derived text-to-speech
models.notes: Text-conditioned speech generation with controllable delivery.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS (text-to-speech) preview | Gemini API | Google AI for Developers
Speech generation (text-to-speech) | Gemini API

models.description: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS adds expressive audio tags to prompt-steered speech generation, giving authors more local control over narration and delivery. It targets natural, responsive multilingual synthesis through a managed API. The public preview documentation describes the interface and controls, without enough architectural detail to reconstruct the underlying speech generator.

models.name: GLM-TTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive token model and diffusion decoder
models.notes: Post-training improves controllable pronunciation, speaker similarity and prosody.

sources.title: GLM-TTS Technical Report
zai-org/GLM-TTS — official repository

models.description: GLM-TTS first predicts speech tokens autoregressively, then converts them into audio with a diffusion decoder. Pitch-aware tokenization and multi-reward reinforcement learning target pronunciation, speaker similarity and expression. Hybrid phoneme/text input and LoRA voice adaptation provide controls for applications that need repeatable pronunciation and customized voices.

models.name: GPT-4o Mini TTS
models.architecture: GPT-derived speech synthesizer
models.notes: Generates spoken audio from text and delivery instructions.

sources.title: GPT-4o Mini TTS
Text to speech | OpenAI API

models.description: GPT-4o Mini TTS combines the text to be spoken with instructions that steer accent, speed, tone and emotional delivery. The Speech API can stream audio before the full result is complete and supports several output formats. It provides a managed synthesis component for narration and voice applications; public documentation does not disclose the complete acoustic architecture.

models.name: GPT-SoVITS
models.architecture: Text-to-semantic GPT and speech decoder
models.notes: Few-shot and zero-shot synthesis using reference audio; the WebUI's separate ASR tools are not part of its language model.

sources.title: RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS — official repository
GPT-SoVITS changelog

models.description: GPT-SoVITS couples text-to-semantic token prediction with a reference-conditioned speech decoder. Its 2025 V3, V4 and V2 Pro releases extend a workflow that supports both zero-shot synthesis and voice adaptation from a small training set. The surrounding WebUI helps prepare data, while recognition and source-separation utilities remain separate components.

models.name: Higgs Audio v2
models.architecture: Text/audio language model with audio heads
models.notes: Text and acoustic context condition expressive speech generation.

sources.title: bosonai/higgs-tts-2-3b-base · Hugging Face

models.description: Higgs Audio v2 combines interleaved text/audio modeling with a unified speech tokenizer and DualFFN layers for acoustic prediction. Reference clips and scene context influence voices, while text context shapes prosody across narration and multi-speaker scripts. The generation checkpoint covers synthesis; the separate understanding branch in the family diagram is not another output mode of this checkpoint.

models.name: Higgs Audio v2.5
models.architecture: Autoregressive audio Transformer with GRPO alignment
models.notes: Successor synthesis release in the Higgs Audio line.

sources.title: Boson AI Launches Higgs TTS 2.5 Voice Model – Boson AI

models.description: Higgs Audio v2.5, now documented as Higgs TTS 2.5, reduces the autoregressive audio Transformer to 1B parameters. GRPO-based alignment and a curated voice dataset refine pronunciation, cloning and expressive control tags. It targets production narration and conversational speech with lower computational requirements than the preceding 3B generation model.

models.name: Higgs Audio v3 TTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive Transformer with delayed audio codebooks
models.notes: Standalone successor with voice conditioning and text-controlled delivery.

sources.title: bosonai/higgs-tts-3-4b · Hugging Face

models.description: Higgs TTS 3 uses an autoregressive decoder over interleaved text and eight speech codebooks, with a delay pattern and fused input/output projections. Reference audio establishes a voice, while inline tokens control emotion, style, pauses and sound effects. The 4B release targets multilingual conversational speech and expressive response rendering.

models.name: Hume Octave TTS
models.architecture: LLM-based expressive speech synthesis
models.notes: Commercial TTS interface with voice design and reference conditioning; EVI 4-mini combines it with an external language model.

sources.title: Text-to-Speech (TTS) | Hume API

models.description: Octave uses text context and acting instructions to adjust pronunciation, emphasis, tempo and emotional delivery. Its API supports voice creation from descriptions, voice cloning and continuation across longer passages. Octave 1 and the Octave 2 preview have different feature coverage; the public interface is documented more fully than the internal speech-model architecture.

models.name: IndexTTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive acoustic generation
models.notes: Extends the XTTS/Tortoise approach with improved pronunciation control.

sources.title: IndexTTS: An Industrial-Level Controllable and Efficient Zero-Shot Text-To-Speech System
IndexTTS author repository
IndexTTS author demo

models.description: IndexTTS adapts the XTTS/Tortoise approach with a Conformer reference encoder and a BigVGAN2 speech decoder. Hybrid character/pinyin input gives explicit control over difficult Chinese pronunciations. Its central use case is zero-shot voice cloning with predictable text rendering, including content that benefits from pronunciation correction.

models.name: IndexTTS 2.5
models.architecture: Text-to-semantic LM and non-AR acoustic decoder
models.notes: Extends IndexTTS2 with multilingual coverage and efficiency improvements.

sources.title: IndexTTS 2.5 Technical Report
IndexTTS 2.5 author repository

models.description: IndexTTS 2.5 shortens semantic sequences with a lower-rate codec and replaces the acoustic module's backbone with a Zipformer design. Multilingual training strategies and reinforcement learning extend pronunciation and emotion transfer across languages. It retains reference-based voice conditioning while reducing the cost of semantic and acoustic generation.

models.name: IndexTTS2
models.architecture: Duration-controlled autoregressive synthesis
models.notes: Separates emotion and timbre control and adds explicit duration conditioning.

sources.title: IndexTTS2: A Breakthrough in Emotionally Expressive and Duration-Controlled Auto-Regressive Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
IndexTTS2 author repository

models.description: IndexTTS2 separates speaker identity from emotional style so that different references can control timbre and delivery. Its autoregressive formulation also supports explicit output-token budgeting for duration control, alongside unconstrained generation. These mechanisms are intended for expressive speech and timing-sensitive work such as dubbing; availability of controls should be checked in the chosen implementation.

models.name: Kyutai TTS (DSM)
models.architecture: Delayed Streams Modeling
models.notes: Aligns text and audio streams with controlled delays for incremental synthesis.

sources.title: Streaming Sequence-to-Sequence Learning with Delayed Streams Modeling
kyutai-labs/delayed-streams-modeling — official repository

models.description: Kyutai TTS treats text and speech as aligned streams separated by a controlled delay. A decoder-only language model can therefore emit audio as text arrives, instead of waiting for a complete utterance. This formulation supports incremental synthesis for voice interfaces and long streams, with speaker conditioning supplied through the TTS implementation.

models.name: Llasa
models.architecture: Single-codebook codec and Llama
models.notes: Uses a single Transformer for language-model-based speech synthesis.

sources.title: Llasa: Scaling Train-Time and Inference-Time Compute for Llama-based Speech Synthesis
Llasa author repository
Llasa author demo

models.description: Llasa maps text and an optional speech prompt to a single stream of codec tokens using a Llama-style Transformer. The simple representation makes standard language-model scaling and sampling techniques applicable to synthesis. Its research also explores speech-model verifiers that select samples for content accuracy, voice consistency or emotional expression.

models.name: Llasa+
models.architecture: Llasa with multi-token prediction
models.notes: Adds acceleration modules and streaming synthesis to the Llasa backbone.

sources.title: Llasa+: Free Lunch for Accelerated and Streaming Llama-Based Speech Synthesis
Llasa+ author repository

models.description: Llasa+ adds multi-token prediction modules to a frozen Llasa backbone and checks their proposals with that backbone. A causal codec decoder turns accepted tokens into streaming audio. The resulting design addresses autoregressive latency while retaining the original speech model, making it relevant to systems that need incremental playback without retraining an entire backbone.

models.name: MaskGCT
models.architecture: Masked generative codec transformers
models.notes: Non-autoregressive token language modeling without explicit text-speech alignment.

sources.title: MaskGCT: Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech with Masked Generative Codec Transformer

models.architecture: Disentangled speech factors and prosody LM
models.notes: Uses separate inductive biases for content, timbre, prosody and waveform generation.

sources.title: Mega-TTS: Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech at Scale with Intrinsic Inductive Bias

models.name: Mega-TTS 2
models.architecture: Prosody language model and multi-sentence prompting
models.notes: Improves prompt utilization and transfer of speaking style.

sources.title: Mega-TTS 2: Boosting Prompting Mechanisms for Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis

models.name: MiniMax-Speech
models.architecture: Autoregressive Transformer and Flow-VAE
models.notes: Learnable speaker conditioning supports expressive multilingual TTS.

sources.title: MiniMax-Speech: Intrinsic Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech with a Learnable Speaker Encoder

models.description: MiniMax-Speech extracts speaker characteristics directly from reference audio without requiring its transcript, then generates speech with an autoregressive Transformer and Flow-VAE. The research emphasizes multilingual zero-shot cloning and expressive delivery. Additional adaptation mechanisms support emotion control, description-based voice creation and more specialized voice cloning without replacing the base model.

models.name: MOSS-TTS
models.architecture: Delay-pattern LM and local Transformer alternatives
models.notes: Family includes structurally distinct generators over MOSS audio tokens.

sources.title: MOSS-TTS Technical Report
OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS — official repository

models.description: MOSS-TTS offers two generators over a shared discrete audio representation: a delay-pattern model and a model with a frame-local Transformer. They balance long-context control against efficient codebook prediction and speaker preservation. The family supports reference-conditioned synthesis, pronunciation and duration controls, with later checkpoints extending language handling and explicit pauses.

models.name: MOSS-TTS-Nano
models.architecture: Compact speech language model
models.notes: Lightweight member of the MOSS-TTS family.

sources.title: OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS — official repository
MOSS-TTS-Nano — official implementation

models.description: MOSS-TTS-Nano packages multilingual voice cloning into a roughly 100M-parameter speech generator with a compact audio tokenizer. Streaming output and an ONNX inference path make it relevant to CPU-based readers and local applications. Its published performance depends on the runtime and hardware, and the tokenizer is a separate part of the deployment footprint.

models.name: MOSS-TTS-Realtime
models.architecture: Streaming autoregressive speech generator
models.notes: The real-time TTS specialization of the MOSS speech-generation family.

sources.title: OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS — official repository
MOSS-TTS-Realtime — model and inference guide

models.description: MOSS-TTS-Realtime uses a Qwen3-derived backbone for linguistic context and a smaller local Transformer to predict audio codebooks. Text and speech tokens are handled at different levels so the system can accept text and emit audio incrementally. It targets low-latency spoken responses while preserving context across the generated utterance.

models.name: MOSS-TTSD
models.architecture: Long-context dialogue speech LM
models.notes: Turns speaker-tagged scripts into multi-party spoken dialogue.

sources.title: MOSS-TTSD: Text to Spoken Dialogue Generation
MOSS-TTSD author repository

models.description: MOSS-TTSD turns a dialogue script with explicit speaker tags into a continuous multi-party recording. Long-context modeling helps maintain speaker identity, turn assignment and acoustic continuity, while short references can define voices. It is designed for podcasts, commentary and other scripted conversations; the source paper evaluates dialogue-specific consistency as well as intelligibility.

models.name: MOSS-VoiceGenerator
models.architecture: Instruction-conditioned voice generation
models.notes: Creates speaking voices from natural-language descriptions.

sources.title: MOSS-VoiceGenerator: Create Realistic Voices with Natural Language Descriptions
MOSS-VoiceGenerator author repository

models.description: MOSS-VoiceGenerator creates a speaking voice from a natural-language description rather than requiring an example speaker recording. Training on expressive cinematic speech exposes it to varied delivery and acoustic conditions. The model is intended for character design, storytelling and role-based narration where the desired voice must be specified in words.

models.name: OmniVoice
models.architecture: Discrete diffusion language model
models.notes: Omnilingual TTS over multiple acoustic codebooks; its name does not imply vision input.

sources.title: OmniVoice: Towards Omnilingual Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech with Diffusion Language Models
k2-fsa/OmniVoice — official repository

models.description: OmniVoice predicts multiple acoustic codebooks directly from text using a masked, non-autoregressive diffusion language model. Random masking across codebooks and initialization from a pretrained language model support multilingual generation without a separate text-to-semantic stage. It focuses on broad-language zero-shot synthesis and voice conditioning, rather than visual or general-purpose omni interaction.

models.name: Orpheus TTS
models.architecture: Llama-based codec language model
models.notes: Expressive synthesis with textual emotion cues and voice conditioning.

sources.title: canopyai/Orpheus-TTS — official repository

models.description: Orpheus TTS repurposes a Llama-family language model to generate speech codec tokens from text. Emotion tags and speaker conditioning guide expressive delivery, while the project supplies inference and adaptation workflows. English releases and multilingual previews have different coverage, so a checkpoint's documented capabilities matter when selecting it for narration or a voice application.

models.name: OuteTTS
models.architecture: Decoder-only speech-token LM
models.notes: TTS models usable through standard LLM inference backends.

sources.title: edwko/OuteTTS — official repository

models.description: OuteTTS represents speech in a form that can be generated by a decoder-only language model and reconstructed by an audio decoder. A speaker reference guides vocal identity, style and accent. Its 1.0 line supports standard LLM serving backends, but generation settings and repetition handling need to follow the matching model implementation.

models.name: Parler-TTS
models.architecture: Description-conditioned codec language model
models.notes: Uses text descriptions of the speaker and delivery to guide synthesis.

sources.title: huggingface/parler-tts — official repository
Natural language guidance of high-fidelity text-to-speech with synthetic annotations

models.name: Pocket TTS
models.architecture: Continuous autoregressive FlowLM
models.notes: Small streaming synthesizer derived from continuous audio language modeling.

sources.title: kyutai-labs/pocket-tts — official repository
Continuous Audio Language Models

models.description: Pocket TTS uses continuous autoregressive speech modeling with a flow-based output mechanism, avoiding long sequences of discrete acoustic codebooks. It combines a small language-model backbone with streaming audio reconstruction and reusable voice conditioning. The project targets CPU-based speech synthesis; language-specific models and runtime choices affect its speed and voice behavior.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS
models.architecture: Dual-track speech language model
models.notes: Family offers voice cloning, preset voices and description-driven voice creation; input conditioning depends on variant.

sources.title: Qwen3-TTS Technical Report
QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS — official repository

models.description: Qwen3-TTS combines a dual-track speech language model with tokenizers designed for compact streaming audio. The released 12Hz line separates Base voice cloning, CustomVoice preset-speaker control and VoiceDesign creation from descriptions. These variants support different conditioning interfaces, allowing applications to choose between reproducing a reference voice and directing a new voice through text.

models.name: RALL-E
models.architecture: Prosody-guided codec language modeling
models.notes: Predicts pitch and duration as intermediate conditions for speech synthesis.

sources.title: RALL-E: Robust Codec Language Modeling with Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Text-to-Speech Synthesis

models.notes: Research family with controllable synthesis and speaker prompting.

sources.title: Seed-TTS: A Family of High-Quality Versatile Speech Generation Models

models.name: Spark-TTS
models.architecture: Qwen2.5 and single-stream BiCodec
models.notes: Separates semantic tokens from global speaker tokens for controllable synthesis.

sources.title: Spark-TTS: An Efficient LLM-Based Text-to-Speech Model with Single-Stream Decoupled Speech Tokens
SparkAudio/Spark-TTS — official repository

models.description: Spark-TTS uses BiCodec to separate changing linguistic content from global speaker attributes, then predicts these tokens with a Qwen2.5 backbone. That separation supports both reference-based cloning and direct control of attributes such as speaking rate and pitch. It is useful for controllable speech generation where a reference recording alone is insufficient to specify the desired delivery.

models.name: SPEAR-TTS
models.architecture: Text-to-semantic and semantic-to-acoustic LMs
models.notes: Separates reading and speaking to reduce paired-data requirements.

sources.title: Speak, Read and Prompt: High-Fidelity Text-to-Speech with Minimal Supervision

models.notes: This card covers the TTS path of the shared speech/text encoder-decoder. ASR and voice conversion are other tasks of the broader model.

sources.title: SpeechT5: Unified-Modal Encoder-Decoder Pre-Training for Spoken Language Processing

models.architecture: Prompted neural codec language model
models.notes: This card covers the text-to-speech path. The broader codec language model also supports speech editing, enhancement and other transformations.

sources.title: SpeechX: Neural Codec Language Model as a Versatile Speech Transformer

models.name: Step-Audio-TTS
models.architecture: Speech-token language model
models.notes: Dedicated synthesizer distributed with Step-Audio; separate from Step-Audio-Chat.

sources.title: Step-Audio: Unified Understanding and Generation in Intelligent Speech Interaction
Step-Audio — official implementation

models.description: Step-Audio-TTS is the compact synthesis component produced through the broader Step-Audio speech-data and distillation pipeline. Text and voice conditioning drive speech-token generation, while the released workflow exposes delivery controls. The TTS checkpoint is used to render supplied content; reasoning, tool use and dialogue management belong to other components of the system.

models.architecture: Autoregressive transformer and diffusion decoder
models.notes: Reference-conditioned synthesis from a scaled generative speech pipeline.

models.notes: Treats synthesis as conditional prediction of neural codec tokens.

models.description: VibeVoice autoregressively generates continuous speech latents with a diffusion head, using compressed acoustic and semantic representations to extend context. It targets long, multi-speaker recordings in which voices and delivery should remain coherent across a script. The original research studies recordings lasting up to 90 minutes with four speakers; those limits do not describe every family variant.

models.name: VibeVoice-Realtime
models.architecture: Streaming next-token diffusion
models.notes: Incremental text-to-speech member of the VibeVoice family.

sources.title: microsoft/VibeVoice — official repository
VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B Model Card

models.description: VibeVoice-Realtime interleaves incoming text chunks with diffusion-based acoustic generation so playback can begin while more text is arriving. The smaller 0.5B design keeps the acoustic tokenizer and removes the semantic tokenizer used by the longer-form model. It focuses on single-speaker streaming, with preset voice embeddings and experimental language coverage documented separately.

models.name: VoiceCraft

models.notes: Supports both speech editing and reference-conditioned TTS.

models.notes: Tokenizer-free speech generation with voice conditioning.

VoxCPM author repository
VoxCPM author demo

models.description: VoxCPM divides synthesis into semantic/prosodic planning and residual acoustic modeling, then uses a local diffusion decoder to produce continuous speech latents. These components are trained together without an external discrete speech tokenizer. Reference conditioning supports voice cloning, while text context helps determine the rhythm and expressive shape of the generated utterance.

models.name: VoxCPM2
models.architecture: Hierarchical diffusion-autoregressive model
models.notes: Extends VoxCPM with multilingual generation and description-based voice control.

sources.title: VoxCPM2 Technical Report
OpenBMB/VoxCPM — official repository
VoxCPM2 author demo

models.description: VoxCPM2 expands the same hierarchical approach to multilingual synthesis, voice design and style-controlled cloning within one backbone. An asymmetric AudioVAE encodes lower-rate audio and reconstructs higher-rate output, while a unified input sequence expresses the different generation tasks. It serves applications that need both reference-based voices and description-driven control from one model family.

models.name: XTTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive acoustic codes and decoder
models.notes: Multilingual reference-conditioned TTS derived from Tortoise.

sources.title: XTTS: a Massively Multilingual Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech Model

models.name: Zonos
models.architecture: Transformer or hybrid backbone with codec prediction
models.notes: Speech synthesis conditioned on text, speaker references and delivery attributes.

sources.title: Zyphra/Zonos — official repository

models.description: Zonos phonemizes text and predicts DAC codec tokens with either a Transformer or a hybrid backbone. Speaker embeddings and audio prefixes condition the voice, alongside explicit controls for rate, pitch variation and emotion. Its v0.1 variants provide alternative architectures for expressive multilingual synthesis and reference-based cloning.

models.name: Tacotron
models.architecture: Attention-based recurrent spectrogram synthesis
models.notes: Maps characters to mel and linear spectrograms, then reconstructs a waveform with Griffin-Lim.

sources.title: Tacotron: Towards End-to-End Speech Synthesis

models.name: Tacotron 2
models.architecture: Recurrent attention model and WaveNet vocoder
models.notes: Predicts mel spectrograms from characters before waveform synthesis with a separately trained neural vocoder.

sources.title: Natural TTS Synthesis by Conditioning WaveNet on Mel Spectrogram Predictions

models.name: Deep Voice
models.architecture: Neural TTS pipeline with autoregressive WaveNet synthesis
models.notes: Combines grapheme-to-phoneme, duration and pitch models with a waveform generator. Segmentation is used during training.

sources.title: Deep Voice: Real-time Neural Text-to-Speech

models.name: Deep Voice 2
models.architecture: Speaker-conditioned neural pipeline and WaveNet synthesis
models.notes: Extends Deep Voice with speaker embeddings and improved components. The paper also evaluates a separate multi-speaker Tacotron system.

sources.title: Deep Voice 2: Multi-Speaker Neural Text-to-Speech

models.name: Deep Voice 3
models.architecture: Convolutional attention encoder-decoder and converter
models.notes: Autoregressively predicts acoustic features; a converter prepares the representation required by the selected waveform synthesizer.

sources.title: Deep Voice 3: Scaling Text-to-Speech with Convolutional Sequence Learning

models.name: Transformer TTS
models.architecture: Autoregressive Transformer and WaveNet vocoder
models.notes: Replaces recurrent layers with multi-head attention in the text-to-mel model. Parallel training does not make its speech decoding non-autoregressive.

sources.title: Neural Speech Synthesis with Transformer Network

models.name: FastSpeech
models.architecture: Feed-forward Transformer and duration-based length regulator
models.notes: Generates mel frames in parallel using durations learned from an autoregressive teacher, followed by a vocoder.

sources.title: FastSpeech: Fast, Robust and Controllable Text to Speech

models.name: FastSpeech 2
models.architecture: Parallel Transformer with duration, pitch and energy prediction
models.notes: Learns from ground-truth speech without teacher distillation. FastSpeech 2s adds a parallel waveform decoder.

sources.title: FastSpeech 2: Fast and High-Quality End-to-End Text to Speech

models.name: FastPitch
models.architecture: Parallel Transformer with explicit pitch prediction
models.notes: Predicts token durations and pitch before mel-spectrogram generation; pitch predictions can be edited to control delivery.

sources.title: FastPitch: Parallel Text-to-speech with Pitch Prediction

models.name: Parallel Tacotron
models.architecture: Parallel acoustic model with a variational residual encoder
models.notes: Uses lightweight convolutions and residual variation modeling to generate mel spectrograms, followed by a neural vocoder.

sources.title: Parallel Tacotron: Non-Autoregressive and Controllable TTS

models.name: Parallel Tacotron 2
models.architecture: Parallel synthesis with differentiable duration modeling
models.notes: Learns alignment and token durations through differentiable upsampling and a Soft-DTW reconstruction objective.

sources.title: Parallel Tacotron 2: A Non-Autoregressive Neural TTS Model with Differentiable Duration Modeling

models.name: SpeedySpeech
models.architecture: Residual convolutional acoustic model with duration expansion
models.notes: A teacher provides durations for the parallel student; a MelGAN vocoder converts predicted spectrograms to audio.

sources.title: SpeedySpeech: Efficient Neural Speech Synthesis

models.name: LightSpeech
models.architecture: FastSpeech-derived architecture found by neural architecture search
models.notes: Searches lightweight convolutional and attention components for compact acoustic modeling. This entry covers the Luo et al. model.

sources.title: LightSpeech: Lightweight and Fast Text to Speech with Neural Architecture Search

models.name: Glow-TTS
models.architecture: Normalizing-flow acoustic model and monotonic alignment search
models.notes: Learns text-to-speech alignment without an external aligner and generates mel spectrograms in parallel before vocoding.

sources.title: Glow-TTS: A Generative Flow for Text-to-Speech via Monotonic Alignment Search

models.name: VITS
models.architecture: Conditional VAE, normalizing flows and adversarial waveform decoding
models.notes: Jointly trains text-to-waveform synthesis with a stochastic duration predictor. Reference-audio cloning is not an intrinsic capability of the original model.

sources.title: Conditional Variational Autoencoder with Adversarial Learning for End-to-End Text-to-Speech

models.name: VITS2
models.architecture: VITS with adversarial duration training and revised flows
models.notes: Improves duration prediction, flow layers and speaker conditioning while reducing dependence on phoneme conversion.

sources.title: VITS2: Improving Quality and Efficiency of Single-Stage Text-to-Speech with Adversarial Learning and Architecture Design

models.name: YourTTS
models.architecture: Multilingual VITS with speaker-reference conditioning
models.notes: Extends VITS for zero-shot multi-speaker synthesis; the broader model also supports voice conversion and speaker adaptation.

sources.title: YourTTS: Towards Zero-Shot Multi-Speaker TTS and Zero-Shot Voice Conversion for everyone

models.name: Flowtron
models.architecture: Autoregressive normalizing flows over mel spectrograms
models.notes: An invertible acoustic model supports sampling and style transfer. A separate vocoder produces the waveform.

sources.title: Flowtron: an Autoregressive Flow-based Generative Network for Text-to-Speech Synthesis

models.name: StyleTTS
models.architecture: Style-conditioned parallel synthesis with a transferable aligner
models.notes: Extracts speaking style from reference speech and predicts duration, pitch and energy for acoustic generation.

sources.title: StyleTTS: A Style-Based Generative Model for Natural and Diverse Text-to-Speech Synthesis

models.name: Grad-TTS
models.architecture: Score-based diffusion decoder and monotonic alignment search
models.notes: Transforms text-conditioned noise into a mel spectrogram; the number of diffusion steps controls the inference tradeoff.

sources.title: Grad-TTS: A Diffusion Probabilistic Model for Text-to-Speech

models.name: Diff-TTS
models.architecture: Text-conditioned denoising diffusion acoustic model
models.notes: Uses a non-autoregressive diffusion process to generate mel spectrograms and accelerated sampling before vocoding.

sources.title: Diff-TTS: A Denoising Diffusion Model for Text-to-Speech

models.name: NaturalSpeech
models.architecture: Text-to-waveform VAE with enhanced prior and duration modeling
models.notes: Combines phoneme pretraining, a differentiable durator, bidirectional prior/posterior modeling and a memory-equipped decoder.

sources.title: NaturalSpeech: End-to-End Text to Speech Synthesis with Human-Level Quality

models.name: NaturalSpeech 2
models.architecture: Latent diffusion over neural-codec representations
models.notes: Speech prompts condition duration, pitch and latent generation for zero-shot synthesis. Singing is an additional task in the paper.

sources.title: NaturalSpeech 2: Latent Diffusion Models are Natural and Zero-Shot Speech and Singing Synthesizers

models.name: NaturalSpeech 3
models.architecture: Factorized speech codec and attribute-wise diffusion
models.notes: Separates content, prosody, timbre and acoustic detail, then generates the corresponding speech representations with diffusion models.

sources.title: NaturalSpeech 3: Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis with Factorized Codec and Diffusion Models

models.name: StyleTTS 2
models.architecture: Style diffusion and adversarial training with speech-model discriminators
models.notes: Samples style conditioned on text; multi-speaker synthesis can additionally use a voice reference. The speech model acts as a discriminator during training.

sources.title: StyleTTS 2: Towards Human-Level Text-to-Speech through Style Diffusion and Adversarial Training with Large Speech Language Models

models.name: Voicebox
models.architecture: Non-autoregressive flow matching for speech infilling
models.notes: Uses text and surrounding audio for zero-shot synthesis. Editing, denoising and style transfer are other applications of the model.

sources.title: Voicebox: Text-Guided Multilingual Universal Speech Generation at Scale

models.name: Matcha-TTS
models.architecture: Conditional flow matching with an encoder-decoder acoustic model
models.notes: An ODE decoder generates mel spectrograms from aligned text representations, followed by a neural vocoder.

sources.title: Matcha-TTS: A fast TTS architecture with conditional flow matching

models.name: F5-TTS
models.architecture: Flow-matching Transformer with ConvNeXt text refinement
models.notes: Pads character sequences to speech length and learns text-guided audio infilling; Sway Sampling adjusts inference steps.

sources.title: F5-TTS: A Fairytaler that Fakes Fluent and Faithful Speech with Flow Matching
F5-TTS — official implementation

models.description: F5-TTS learns text-guided speech infilling with flow matching, refining character representations before a Transformer predicts the speech trajectory. A reference clip supplies voice context, and Sway Sampling controls how inference steps are distributed. The 2025 v1 Base release refines training and inference within the same general architecture for zero-shot speech synthesis.

models.name: E2 TTS
models.architecture: Flow matching with filler-token text conditioning
models.notes: Learns speech infilling without a phoneme aligner or explicit duration predictor. The paper describes alternate input representations.

sources.title: E2 TTS: Embarrassingly Easy Fully Non-Autoregressive Zero-Shot TTS

models.name: DiTTo-TTS
models.architecture: Latent diffusion Transformer with speech-length prediction
models.notes: Uses text conditioning and a total-length predictor instead of phoneme-level durations for zero-shot speech synthesis.

sources.title: DiTTo-TTS: Diffusion Transformers for Scalable Text-to-Speech without Domain-Specific Factors

models.name: MegaTTS 3
models.architecture: Sparse-alignment latent diffusion Transformer
models.notes: Sparse boundaries guide text-speech alignment; piecewise rectified flow accelerates synthesis and guidance controls accent strength.

sources.title: MegaTTS 3: Sparse Alignment Enhanced Latent Diffusion Transformer for Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis
MegaTTS 3 author repository

models.description: MegaTTS 3 guides a latent diffusion Transformer with sparse text-speech alignment boundaries, leaving the model room to learn finer timing. Classifier-free guidance controls accent strength, while piecewise rectified flow reduces sampling work. The design targets robust zero-shot voice synthesis with more flexible alignment than a fully fixed duration sequence.

models.name: PortaSpeech
models.architecture: Variational acoustic model and flow-based post-net
models.notes: Combines word-level and phoneme-level alignment with a lightweight VAE; the post-net restores acoustic detail before vocoding.

sources.title: PortaSpeech: Portable and High-Quality Generative Text-to-Speech

models.name: DelightfulTTS
models.architecture: Conformer acoustic model with explicit and implicit prosody
models.notes: Predicts acoustic features and variation factors, then uses HiFiNet to synthesize higher-sample-rate audio.

sources.title: DelightfulTTS: The Microsoft Speech Synthesis System for Blizzard Challenge 2021

models.name: JETS
models.architecture: Joint FastSpeech 2 and HiFi-GAN with learned alignment
models.notes: Trains the acoustic model and waveform generator together, avoiding a separately supplied text-speech alignment.

sources.title: JETS: Jointly Training FastSpeech2 and HiFi-GAN for End to End Text to Speech

models.name: Mellotron
models.architecture: Tacotron 2 with global style tokens, pitch and rhythm conditioning
models.notes: Reference audio can provide prosody. The broader model also accepts musical-score controls and supports singing synthesis.

sources.title: Mellotron: Multispeaker expressive voice synthesis by conditioning on rhythm, pitch and global style tokens

models.name: GST-Tacotron
models.architecture: Tacotron with a reference encoder and global style tokens
models.notes: Unsupervised style embeddings control delivery; synthesis can use reference audio or manually selected token weights.

sources.title: Style Tokens: Unsupervised Style Modeling, Control and Transfer in End-to-End Speech Synthesis

models.name: Wave-Tacotron
models.architecture: Autoregressive waveform blocks with a normalizing-flow decoder
models.notes: Models long-range dependencies across waveform blocks autoregressively and samples each block with a conditional flow.

sources.title: Wave-Tacotron: Spectrogram-free end-to-end text-to-speech synthesis

models.name: PromptTTS
models.architecture: Style and content text encoders with a speech decoder
models.notes: Accepts a spoken script plus a natural-language description of the desired voice and delivery.

sources.title: PromptTTS: Controllable Text-to-Speech with Text Descriptions

models.name: PromptTTS 2
models.architecture: Prompt-conditioned TTS with a diffusion variation network
models.notes: Samples voice variability not captured by the text description. Reference speech is used in training; the prompt-generation LLM is a separate data-construction component.

sources.title: PromptTTS 2: Describing and Generating Voices with Text Prompt

models.name: Kokoro
models.architecture: StyleTTS 2-derived decoder with iSTFTNet
models.notes: The released 82M model omits style diffusion and a reference encoder; preset voice representations condition synthesis.

sources.title: Kokoro-82M model card

models.description: Kokoro's 2025 v1.0 release uses a compact StyleTTS 2-derived decoder with an iSTFTNet waveform generator. The released model relies on preset voice representations and omits style diffusion and a reference encoder. It is suited to lightweight narration and application speech where a small synthesis model and ready-made voices are useful.

models.name: KittenTTS
models.architecture: Compact neural speech synthesis with ONNX inference
models.notes: The official release provides CPU-oriented models and preset voices. Its README does not fully disclose the internal acoustic architecture.

sources.title: KittenTTS official repository

models.description: KittenTTS provides small ONNX speech models with built-in voices and adjustable playback speed. The Mini, Micro and Nano releases offer different size and inference tradeoffs for CPU-oriented applications. The official README documents usage more fully than internal acoustic design, so the catalog presents it as a compact synthesis family without asserting an undisclosed architecture.

models.name: MeloTTS
models.architecture: VITS-family multilingual speech synthesis
models.notes: The implementation builds on VITS, VITS2 and Bert-VITS2. Language and speaker selections depend on the released checkpoint.

sources.title: MeloTTS official repository

models.name: Piper (VITS voices)
models.architecture: VITS voice models exported for local inference
models.notes: This entry covers the trained voice family distributed through Piper. The runtime and individual voice packs are not counted as separate architectures.

sources.title: Piper official repository
Piper voice training guide

models.name: NeuTTS Air
models.architecture: Compact language-model backbone and single-codebook NeuCodec
models.notes: Phoneme-conditioned voice cloning with quantized local inference; streaming is documented for the GGUF backend.

sources.title: NeuTTS official repository

models.description: NeuTTS Air pairs a phoneme-conditioned language model with NeuCodec to synthesize a reference voice locally. Quantized GGUF backbones support incremental generation through the documented streaming backend. It targets embedded and desktop voice applications, with the codec's compute and memory requirements considered alongside those of the language-model backbone.

models.name: NeuTTS Nano
models.architecture: Smaller speech language model with NeuCodec decoding
models.notes: A smaller phoneme-input family; language-specific checkpoints share an architecture. Streaming is documented for GGUF inference.

sources.title: NeuTTS official repository

models.description: NeuTTS Nano reduces the speech-model backbone while retaining phoneme conditioning, reference-based cloning and NeuCodec reconstruction. Its English, German, French and Spanish models share a design but use separate language-specific checkpoints. Quantized variants support compact local deployments, and streaming depends on the selected inference backend.

models.name: NeuTTS-2E
models.architecture: Text-input speech language model with emotion control
models.notes: Uses fixed speaker presets and emotion controls. The official release documents streaming through GGUF inference.

sources.title: NeuTTS official repository

models.description: NeuTTS-2E accepts text directly and adds explicit emotional delivery to the NeuTTS language-model-and-codec pipeline. The released configuration supplies four fixed speaker presets instead of arbitrary reference-based cloning. It is intended for compact expressive speech applications, with streaming available through the documented GGUF inference path.

models.name: WhisperSpeech
models.architecture: Text-to-semantic and semantic-to-acoustic token models
models.notes: Builds semantic units from Whisper and predicts acoustic tokens for waveform decoding. Voice references condition synthesis; this is separate from Whisper ASR.

sources.title: WhisperSpeech official repository

models.name: EmotiVoice
models.architecture: PromptTTS-derived style and content conditioning
models.notes: Released English and Chinese synthesizers accept text prompts describing emotion and delivery. Voice adaptation is a separate training workflow.

sources.title: EmotiVoice official repository

models.name: Supertonic
models.architecture: Compact latent flow matching with a speech autoencoder and duration predictor
models.notes: The paper supports reference-conditioned synthesis, while the original open-weight ONNX release provides preset English voices. The source date is the research paper's first submission, not the ONNX release date.

sources.title: Supertonic model card
SupertonicTTS: Towards Highly Efficient and Streamlined Text-to-Speech System
Supertonic author repository
Supertonic author demo

models.description: The SupertonicTTS research system compresses speech into continuous latents and predicts them from character-level text with flow matching. ConvNeXt blocks, temporal compression and a separate duration predictor keep synthesis compact. The later Supertonic ONNX release exposes preset voice-style assets; its packaged configurations should not be equated with the paper's 44M-parameter research model.

models.name: Supertonic 2
models.architecture: Multilingual compact speech synthesis with ONNX inference
models.notes: Extends the local preset-voice release to English, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese and French. Voice-style assets condition synthesis.

sources.title: Supertonic 2 model card

models.description: Supertonic 2 extends the local ONNX synthesis line to five languages while retaining voice-style conditioning and a compact model. It provides a practical path to multilingual narration on devices that can run the supplied inference stack. Creating a new voice-style asset is a separate workflow from generating speech with an existing asset.

models.name: Supertonic 3
models.architecture: Compact multilingual synthesis with expression controls
models.notes: The open-weight package includes preset voices and expression tags across 31 languages. Creating custom voice-style assets is a separate service workflow.

sources.title: Supertonic 3 model card

models.description: Supertonic 3 expands language coverage and adds expression tags while keeping local ONNX inference and preset voice styles. The release targets more reliable reading across short and long text, with controls for events such as breaths or laughter. Custom voice-style creation is offered through a separate service; downloaded styles can then condition local synthesis.

models.name: CDE-StyleTTS
models.architecture: Duration-aware neural controlled differential equations
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Continuous-Time Acoustic Modelling with Neural Controlled Differential Equations
CDE-StyleTTS author repository

models.description: CDE-StyleTTS lets acoustic states evolve continuously along a phoneme sequence whose timing comes from durations. Sampling this trajectory supplies the acoustic decoder with timing-sensitive representations, providing a way to transfer changing expressive style instead of merely repeating phoneme embeddings.

models.name: AuK
models.architecture: Instruction-conditioned hybrid rectified-flow Transformer
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: AuK Technical Report: An Open-Source Foundational Model for Speech Generation and Editing
AuK author repository

models.description: AuK combines language-model conditioning, an audio VAE and successive multimodal and single-stream diffusion blocks. One model handles reference-based speech synthesis and instruction-guided editing; its distilled AuK-Flash variant reduces the number of generation steps.

models.name: TontaubeV1
models.architecture: Hierarchical codec prediction with bounded streaming context
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: TontaubeV1: Streaming Text-to-Speech with Hierarchical Codec Modeling and Bounded Context
TontaubeV1 author repository

models.description: TontaubeV1 assigns a large Transformer to semantic speech tokens and smaller Transformers to successive acoustic refinements. Character-level text, synchronized position markers and a causal waveform reconstruction path support long recordings and streaming voice cloning, primarily in English and German.

models.name: KABURI-TTS
models.architecture: Phoneme-raster and activity-conditioned two-channel synthesis
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: KABURI-TTS: Phoneme-Keyed Activity-conditioned Bi-channel Utterance Rendering for Interaction

models.description: KABURI-TTS renders each participant on a separate audio channel from time-aligned phonemes and speaker activity. Supplying the timing layout explicitly lets the system synthesize overlapping speech, backchannels and interruptions for two-speaker conversations.

models.name: FireRedAudio
models.architecture: Shared language model with separate continuous speech pathways
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: FireRedAudio: A General-Purpose Audio Language Model with Decoupled Continuous Representations for Understanding and Generation
FireRedAudio author repository

models.description: FireRedAudio uses different acoustic encoders for understanding audio and conditioning speech generation. Its shared language model drives a flow-matching decoder over continuous RedAE latents, supporting voice cloning, instruction-controlled synthesis and speech editing within the broader audio model.

models.name: EmoTra-TTS
models.architecture: Language model and flow decoder with time-varying emotion conditioning
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: EmoTra-TTS: Smooth Intra-Utterance Emotion Transitions for Speech Synthesis
EmoTra-TTS author repository
EmoTra-TTS author demo

models.description: EmoTra-TTS introduces frame-level valence, arousal and dominance controls into both prosodic planning and acoustic decoding. Synthetic transition examples teach the model to move between emotions within an utterance while keeping its wording and speaker identity consistent.

models.name: X2Streaming-TTS
models.architecture: Causal streaming codec TTS with speech-state inheritance
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: X2Streaming-TTS: Causal Token-Level Text-to-Speech from Streaming Text with Speech-State Inheritance
X2Streaming-TTS author repository

models.description: X2Streaming-TTS consumes text as it arrives and retains speech-generation state across successive segments. A frontend delays ambiguous text until its pronunciation can be decided, while the talker and waveform decoder produce incremental audio with bounded context.

models.name: FireRedTTS3
models.architecture: Semantic-enriched continuous representations with autoregressive generation
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: FireRedTTS3: Unified Speech Generation and Editing with Semantically Enriched Speech Representations
FireRedTTS3 author repository

models.description: FireRedTTS3 uses a semantically supervised audio autoencoder to make continuous speech representations easier to predict. The Base variant provides multilingual reference cloning; the Instruct variant adds natural-language voice design and editing of spoken content or acoustic attributes.

models.name: VoiceChat-TTS
models.architecture: Continuous autoregressive synthesis driven by streaming text tokens
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: VoiceChat-TTS: A Low-Latency Continuous Speech Synthesis Model for Interactive Agents

models.description: VoiceChat-TTS generates speech directly from an incoming language-model text stream. Control tokens allow interruptions and silence, and generation can resume without discarding the attention cache, making the synthesizer suitable for interactive agent playback.

models.name: VoiceDesigner
models.architecture: Unified diffusion Transformer for voice generation and editing
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: VoiceDesigner: Text-to-Voice Generation and Editing via Unified Diffusion Modeling and Data Augmentation
VoiceDesigner author demo

models.description: VoiceDesigner conditions speech generation on descriptions of a desired voice and supports modifying an existing voice. A shared diffusion model learns these tasks from natural and augmented voice examples, including voices with unusual or fictional characteristics.

models.name: MiDashengLM-Gen
models.architecture: Language-model-driven autoregressive flow matching for mixed audio
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: MiDashengLM-Gen: Unified Audio Scene Generation via LLM-Driven Autoregressive Flow Matching
MiDashengLM-Gen author repository
MiDashengLM-Gen author demo

models.description: MiDashengLM-Gen trains a language model together with a conditional flow-matching output head to generate variable-length audio. Its text conditioning supports scenes containing intelligible speech alongside music or other sounds, with generation performed over continuous audio representations.

models.name: Phoenix TTS
models.architecture: Jointly learned speech tokens with an autoregressive LM and flow decoder
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Phoenix TTS: High-Fidelity Synthesis and Voice Conversion via Flow-Matching-Driven Speech Tokenization

models.description: Phoenix TTS aligns its speech tokenizer with the downstream flow-matching acoustic decoder during training. An autoregressive language model predicts the resulting discrete representation, supporting text-to-speech and voice conversion without separating token design from acoustic reconstruction.

models.name: Confucius4-TTS
models.architecture: Speaker-conditioned text-to-semantic LM and acoustic flow matching
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Confucius4-TTS: Transcript-Free Cross-Lingual Zero-Shot TTS with a Learnable Speaker Encoder
Confucius4-TTS author repository

models.description: Confucius4-TTS extracts voice characteristics from self-supervised speech features without requiring a transcript of the reference recording. A language model predicts semantic tokens and a flow decoder generates mel-spectrograms, enabling voice cloning within and across fourteen languages.

models.name: Luna-TTS
models.architecture: Discrete diffusion language modeling with parallel and block-causal variants
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Luna-TTS Family Technical Report
Luna-TTS author demo

models.description: Luna-TTS adapts an autoregressive text backbone into a speech diffusion language model. Its parallel and Realtime variants share a tokenizer and training lineage; Realtime predicts successive codec blocks while denoising each block in parallel for incremental audio delivery.

models.name: CookVoice
models.architecture: Factorized content, prosody and style with frame-aligned flow synthesis
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: CookVoice: Unified Framework for Style Controllable Multi-Modal Human Voice Generation
CookVoice author demo

models.description: CookVoice aligns textual content, style and prosodic controls to acoustic frames before speech generation. The same compact model supports spoken and sung voices, reference imitation and editing, allowing individual voice attributes to be controlled within a shared synthesis pipeline.

models.name: CuteTTS
models.architecture: Patch-autoregressive continuous latents with a flow-matching head
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: CuteTTS: Efficient and High-Quality Speech Synthesis via Autoregressive Modeling of Continuous Latents
CuteTTS author repository

models.description: CuteTTS combines a causal audio VAE, an autoregressive patch model and an explicitly speaker-conditioned flow head. Generating patches rather than individual frames reduces sequential work; a distilled variant targets faster streaming while preserving reference-voice synthesis.

models.name: CtrlSpeech
models.architecture: DiTAR synthesis with global voice and phoneme-level prosody controls
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: CtrlSpeech: Coarse-to-Fine Control for Expressive Speech Synthesis
CtrlSpeech author repository

models.description: CtrlSpeech adds local pitch, loudness and duration conditioning to a patch-autoregressive diffusion synthesizer. A separate global speaker condition preserves the reference voice while users modify the delivery of individual words or phonemes.

models.name: SemBridge
models.architecture: Semantic-anchored continuous autoregression with an aligned acoustic VAE
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: SemBridge: Semantic Token Anchoring for Continuous-Latent Autoregressive Speech Generation
SemBridge author repository

models.description: SemBridge uses discrete semantic targets during training to organize both acoustic latents and language-model hidden states. The resulting continuous generator supports zero-shot speech synthesis with stronger content alignment, without needing to generate the auxiliary semantic tokens during inference.

models.name: DAIEN-TTS
models.architecture: Disentangled speech and environment prompts in an F5-TTS flow model
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Towards Real-world Environment-aware Zero-shot Text-to-speech Synthesis via Disentangled Audio Infilling
DAIEN-TTS author demo
DAIEN-TTS: Disentangled Audio Infilling for Environment-Aware Text-to-Speech Synthesis
DAIEN-TTS author repository
DAIEN-TTS author demo

models.description: DAIEN-TTS separates a reference recording into speech and environmental components, then conditions acoustic generation on them independently. Its extended formulation additionally models reverberation and uses separate guidance controls for speech, noise and room acoustics, enabling voice cloning into a chosen environment.

models.name: MP-ELD
models.architecture: Multi-path continuous autoregression with residual flow guidance
models.notes: The first-submission date refers to the linked research paper. Reference and control options depend on the synthesis setting described there.

sources.title: Stable Autoregressive Speech Generation with Low-Frame-Rate High-Dimensional Continuous Tokens

models.description: MP-ELD predicts low-rate continuous speech tokens through several information paths with separate local encoders. A flow decoder combines their predictions, while the accompanying Locodec representation is designed to limit accumulated errors during long speech generation.

models.name: Face-adapted StyleTTS 2
models.architecture: Face-to-style adapter over a frozen style-diffusion synthesizer
